audio.description: Output volume, with the default sink and per-application streams in its popover.

scroll-step.description: How much one scroll notch on the speaker icon changes the volume, in percent, from 1 to 100.

tooltip-format.description: What the bar's tooltip reads. `{volume}` is the volume in percent, or Muted.

devices.description: How many paired devices the popover lists before the rest go behind a drawer.

nearby.description: How many nearby devices the popover lists while scanning.

tooltip-format.description:
What the bar's tooltip reads. `{status}` says whether Bluetooth is on and how many devices
are connected, `{devices}` lists the connected devices and `{adapter}` is the adapter's
name.

label-format.description:
What the chip reads beside its icon. `{count}` is the number of entries held. Left unset the
chip is an icon alone, which is what every applet does unless asked otherwise.

preview-chars.description:
How much of an entry a row shows before it is ellipsized, in characters. A row holds 128 at
most and shows roughly 24 before ellipsizing, so this trades tooltip detail for nothing much
on screen. Clamped to 8..=128.

show-when-empty.description:
Whether the chip is shown when nothing has been copied yet. Off, the applet takes no room
until there is something to open it for.

tooltip-format.description:
What the bar's tooltip reads. `{count}` is the number of entries held. Unset shows no
tooltip.

visible.description:
How many recent entries the popover lists. Nothing in the panel scrolls, so this is what
keeps the card on the screen. Pinned entries are listed above and are not counted here —
a pin is an explicit choice and is never dropped from the list. Clamped to 1..=50.

clock.description: The time and date, with a calendar in its popover.

hide-all-day.description:
Whether an all-day entry is left out of the calendar popover's day list entirely, rather
than shown alongside the day's timed events.

label-format.description: A `strftime` format string for the bar, such as `%H:%M` or `%a %d %b %H:%M`.

timezone.description:
The IANA zone this clock reads, such as `UTC` or `Asia/Tokyo`. Unset is the local zone;
naming one is how a second `[applets.clock-utc]` shows somewhere else.

timezones.description: The other zones the popover lists under its world clock. Empty hides the section.

tooltip-format.description:
What the bar's tooltip reads. A `strftime` format, such as `%A, %-d %B %Y`. Unset shows no
tooltip.

week-numbers.description: Whether the popover names the ISO week the shown month belongs to.

color-picker.description: Picks a color from the screen on right click; the popover keeps the picked colors.

tooltip-format.description:
What the bar's tooltip reads. `{color}` is the last picked color, in the notation chosen
in the popover.

command.description: A chip the user defines, running a program on a click or a scroll.

icon.description:
A themed icon name, or the absolute path to an image. Prefer a `-symbolic` name, which
follows the bar's color.

label.description: Text beside the icon. With neither an icon nor a label the chip takes no room.

on-scroll-down.description: What each notch of scrolling down runs, once per notch.

on-scroll-left.description: What each notch of scrolling left runs, once per notch.

on-scroll-right.description: What each notch of scrolling right runs, once per notch.

on-scroll-up.description: What each notch of scrolling up runs, once per notch.

tooltip-format.description: What the bar's tooltip reads. Plain text. Unset shows no tooltip.

display.description: Connected outputs, brightness and night light in one popover.

scroll-step.description:
How much a scroll notch on the chip moves the current display, in percent of its range.
Converted to native units at the call site and rounded away from zero, so a notch always
moves something even on a display with a small native range. Zero would leave the wheel
silently dead; the range is 1 to 100.

tooltip-format.description:
What the bar's tooltip reads. `{name}` is the display's name and `{brightness}` its
brightness in percent.

exec.description: A third-party applet found through its `.desktop` file (`Implements=me.aresa.Glimpse.Applet1`).

applet.description: The desktop-file id, e.g. `me.aresa.GlimpseTodo` for the todo example.

env.description: Variables set for the applet process on top of the panel's environment.

options.description: Passed to the applet as written.

heartbeat.description:
A counter that ticks once a second. A development fixture: it proves the service is
reachable and events are arriving, and is not meant for a real bar.

idle.description: Idle inhibition, for keeping the screen awake.

tooltip-format.description:
What the bar's tooltip reads. `{status}` says what is keeping the screen awake, if
anything.

kdeconnect.description:
A phone paired through KDE Connect: its battery on the bar, and ring, ping, send and pair
in its popover. Needs `kdeconnectd` running; it is never started from here.

device.description:
The device the bar follows, by the name the device announces. Unset follows the first
connected paired device.

hide-when-disconnected.description:
Hide the chip while no paired device is connected, instead of showing it with an offline
emblem.

indicator-style.description: Whether the bar shows the device icon, the label, or both.

label-format.description:
What the label shows. Placeholders are replaced by name: `{name}`, `{battery}` and
`{charging}`. A placeholder with nothing behind it renders as nothing, so a device with no
battery never shows a bare `%`.

tooltip-format.description:
What the bar's tooltip reads. `{name}`, `{battery}` and `{charging}`, the same tokens as
`label-format`. Unset lists every paired device.

keyboard.description: The active keyboard layout, and switches between the configured ones.

tooltip-format.description:
What the bar's tooltip reads. `{code}` is the layout's short label and `{name}` its full
name.

mpris.description: The currently playing track, with transport controls in its popover.

label-format.description:
What the bar shows. Placeholders are replaced by name: `{player}`, `{title}`, `{artist}`,
`{album}`, `{state}`, `{position}`, `{duration}` and `{remaining}`. A placeholder with
nothing behind it renders as nothing.

max-length.description:
Longest label the bar shows, in characters; the rest is ellipsized. Track titles come from
whatever is playing and are unbounded, and a bar that resizes as they change is worse than
one that truncates.

tooltip-format.description: What the bar's tooltip reads. The same tokens as `label-format`. Unset shows no tooltip.

network.description: Connection state, with the available networks in its popover.

tooltip-format.description:
What the bar's tooltip reads. `{connection}` is the network you are on, `{metered}` reads
Metered connection on a metered one, `{signal}` is the Wi-Fi signal in percent and `{vpn}`
the active VPN's name. A line whose tokens are all empty is left out.

visible-networks.description:
How many networks the popover lists before the rest go behind a "more networks" row. `0`
lists every network in range.

vpn-chip.description:
Whether an active VPN gets a chip of its own beside the network chip. An indicator is an
icon, and two states overlaid on one glyph are illegible at bar size.

next-event.description: The next entry from the configured calendars.

all-day.description:
Whether an all-day entry may take the bar. A timed event always wins over one, so this
only decides what happens on a day holding nothing else — leaving it off keeps a week of
leave from pinning the applet open for the whole week.

countdown.description:
How close an event has to be before the bar spells out how long is left, in minutes. Inside
it the indicator reads `Design review in 12 min`, or `ends in 25 min` once it has started;
outside it the title stands alone. Set it below `within` to have an entry appear quietly and
start counting only as it approaches; `0` never counts.

horizon.description:
How far ahead the popover's list reaches, in minutes. This is the second of two windows and
the wider one: `within` decides when the bar lights up, `horizon` decides what the list
holds once you open it. The default 720 is twelve hours, so a late-afternoon glance still
reaches tomorrow morning — a plain "today only" rule empties the list at exactly the hour
tomorrow's first meeting starts mattering. 1440 is a rolling day.

tooltip-format.description:
What the bar's tooltip reads. `{summary}` is the event's title, `{detail}` its location or
description, `{when}` when it starts and `{conflicts}` the events overlapping it. Unset
shows no tooltip.

upcoming.description:
How many entries the popover lists under the one it is showing, whichever `horizon` leaves.
Capped at 20, because a list longer than that is a popover taller than the screen.

within.description:
How long before an event starts it takes the bar, in minutes. Anything further out than
this leaves the applet empty, which is what keeps a meeting two days away off a bar that
has nothing to say about it. An event that has already started stays until it ends,
however long it has been running, so `0` shows only what is under way.

notifications.description: Unread notifications, with their history in its popover.

indicator-style.description:
How the bar marks unread notifications: `icon-dot` adds a dot, `icon-counter` shows how many,
`icon-only` shows the bell alone.

tooltip-format.description:
What the bar's tooltip reads. `{count}` is the number of unread notifications. Unset says
how many are waiting and whether do not disturb is on.

pager.description: A strip of workspaces or windows, one slot each, that switches between them on a click.

focused-label.description:
The label for the slot the user is on, so the current workspace can show its name while
the rest stay numbers. Same tokens as `label`; unset falls back to it.

label.description:
What a slot reads, when the shape is `labels`, and the fallback for every state below.
Understands `{index}`, `{id}`, `{name}`, `{name-or-index}` and `{workspace-name}`.
`{index}` falls back to the id, because only niri numbers its workspaces separately from
their ids; in `windows` mode it is the slot's position and `{name}` is the window's app
id, which is why `{workspace-name}` exists.

mode.description: Whether each slot is a workspace or a window.

scope.description: How much of the session the strip covers.

shape.description: Whether a slot is drawn as a dot or as its label in a pill.

unfocused-label.description:
The label for every slot the user is not on. Same tokens as `label`; unset falls back
to it.

urgent-label.description:
The label for a slot asking for attention. Takes precedence over the other two, because a
window wanting attention is the one thing the strip exists to surface. Same tokens as
`label`; unset falls back to it.

places.description: Home and user directories, bookmarks, network shares and the trash.

bookmarks.description: How many bookmarks the popover lists before the rest go behind a drawer.

tooltip-format.description:
What the bar's tooltip reads. `{bookmarks}` and `{places}` are how many of each the popover
lists.

power.description: Battery, power mode, keep awake and peripheral batteries in its popover.

indicator-style.description: Whether the bar shows the battery icon, the label, or both.

label-format.description:
What the label shows. Placeholders are replaced by name: `{percentage}`, `{state}` and
`{remaining}`, the time left to empty or full.

tooltip-format.description:
What the bar's tooltip reads. `{percentage}`, `{state}` and `{remaining}`, the time left
until empty or full.

jobs.description: Print jobs listed in the popover before older ones are hidden.

show.description: When the bar shows the printing chip.

tooltip-format.description:
What the bar's tooltip reads. `{document}` is the document printing now, `{printer}` the
printer, `{pages}` how far it has got and `{count}` how many jobs are waiting. Shown only
while something is printing. A line whose tokens are all empty is left out.

privacy.description: Shows when the microphone, camera or screen is in use.

show-camera.description: Whether the camera is shown when in use.

show-location.description: Whether location access is shown when in use.

show-microphone.description: Whether the microphone is shown when in use.

show-screencast.description: Whether screen capture is shown when in use.

tooltip-format.description: What the bar's tooltip reads. Plain text. Unset names what is in use and by which app.

removable.description: Removable drives, one row each, with open and eject in its popover.

tooltip-format.description: What the bar's tooltip reads. `{drives}` and `{volumes}` are how many of each are attached.

volumes.description:
How many devices (drives, not their volumes) the popover lists before the rest go behind a
drawer.

ruler.description: Measures a distance on screen on right click; the popover keeps recent measurements.

tooltip-format.description: What the bar's tooltip reads. `{measurement}` is the last distance measured.

session.description: Log out, suspend, restart and shut down.

tooltip-format.description: What the bar's tooltip reads. `{user}` is your user name.

system-monitor.description:
Live CPU, RAM, swap, disk, network and (amdgpu) GPU load. Nothing is sampled unless the
applet is on a panel.

chip-format.description:
How each chip's own label reads. `{name}` is the chip's own localized name ("CPU", "RAM",
…); `{value}` is its reading ("42%" for a percentage chip, "↓1.2 MB/s" for network, "62°C" for a
temperature). An
unrecognized token is left as literal text rather than silently emptied.

chips.description:
Chips shown on the bar, in order. Anything sampled but left out here still appears in the
popover — this list is panel real estate, not visibility. A repeated chip collapses to its
first occurrence.

critical-percent.description:
Percent at and above which a percentage reading is shown as critical. Must not be below
`warn-percent`.

tooltip-format.description: What the bar's tooltip reads. Plain text, the same on every chip. Unset shows no tooltip.

warn-percent.description:
Percent at and above which a percentage reading (CPU, RAM, swap, GPU usage and memory) is
shown as a warning. Network and temperatures have no percentage and are never colored.

tray.description: The system tray: icons from applications that ask for one.

hide.description:
Item ids never shown, matched against the application's own `Id`. That id survives an
application restart, which the bus name it happens to hold does not.

max-visible.description:
How many icons stay on the bar; the rest open from the chevron beside them. `0` keeps every
icon on the bar and shows no chevron.

pin.description:
Item ids kept on the bar whatever the cap, in the order given. Anything not named here
follows in the order the items registered.

weather.description: Current conditions, with the forecast in its popover.

days.description:
How many days after today the popover's list shows. Today always leads the list, holding
the current conditions.

hours.description:
How many hours the popover's strip shows. The strip starts at the next hour — the hour
standing is already the hero.

label.description:
What the bar and the popover call this place. Unset means a fixed place reads as the pair
it was given, and `here` as whatever the geolocation service resolved.

tooltip-format.description: What the bar's tooltip reads. `{place}`, `{temperature}`, `{feels-like}` and `{condition}`.

widget-demo.description:
A popover with a colored block in every slot of the shell. A development fixture, mirrored by
`sdk/examples/widget_demo`, for comparing built-in and exec rendering; not meant for a real bar.

workspace-name.description: The current workspace's name, renamed from its popover.

tooltip-format.description:
What the bar's tooltip reads. `{index}`, `{id}`, `{name}`, `{name-or-index}` and
`{workspace-name}`, the same tokens as the pager's `label`. Unset shows the workspace
and its monitor.

oneOf.description: Output volume, with the default sink and per-application streams in its popover.

scroll-step.description: How much one scroll notch on the speaker icon changes the volume, in percent, from 1 to 100.

tooltip-format.description: What the bar's tooltip reads. `{volume}` is the volume in percent, or Muted.

oneOf.description: Battery, power mode, keep awake and peripheral batteries in its popover.

label-format.description:

`{remaining}`, the time left to empty or full.

tooltip-format.description:
What the bar's tooltip reads. `{percentage}`, `{state}` and `{remaining}`, the time left
until empty or full.

tooltip-format.description: What the bar's tooltip reads. `{user}` is your user name.

oneOf.description:
Live CPU, RAM, swap, disk, network and (amdgpu) GPU load. Nothing is sampled unless the
applet is on a panel.

chip-format.description:
How each chip's own label reads. `{name}` is the chip's own localized name ("CPU", "RAM",
…); `{value}` is its reading ("42%" for a percentage chip, "↓1.2 MB/s" for network, "62°C" for a
temperature). An
unrecognized token is left as literal text rather than silently emptied.

chips.description:
Chips shown on the bar, in order. Anything sampled but left out here still appears in the
popover — this list is panel real estate, not visibility. A repeated chip collapses to its
first occurrence.

critical-percent.description:
Percent at and above which a percentage reading is shown as critical. Must not be below
`warn-percent`.

tooltip-format.description: What the bar's tooltip reads. Plain text, the same on every chip. Unset shows no tooltip.

warn-percent.description:
Percent at and above which a percentage reading (CPU, RAM, swap, GPU usage and memory) is
shown as a warning. Network and temperatures have no percentage and are never colored.

oneOf.description: The system tray: icons from applications that ask for one.

hide.description:
Item ids never shown, matched against the application's own `Id`. That id survives an
application restart, which the bus name it happens to hold does not.

max-visible.description:
How many icons stay on the bar; the rest open from the chevron beside them. `0` keeps every
icon on the bar and shows no chevron.

pin.description:
Item ids kept on the bar whatever the cap, in the order given. Anything not named here
follows in the order the items registered.

oneOf.description: Current conditions, with the forecast in its popover.

days.description:
How many days after today the popover's list shows. Today always leads the list, holding
the current conditions.

hours.description:
How many hours the popover's strip shows. The strip starts at the next hour — the hour
standing is already the hero.

label.description:
What the bar and the popover call this place. Unset means a fixed place reads as the pair
it was given, and `here` as whatever the geolocation service resolved.

tooltip-format.description: What the bar's tooltip reads. `{place}`, `{temperature}`, `{feels-like}` and `{condition}`.

oneOf.description:
A popover with a colored block in every slot of the shell. A development fixture, mirrored by
`sdk/examples/widget_demo`, for comparing built-in and exec rendering; not meant for a real bar.
The current workspace's name, renamed from its popover.

tooltip-format.description:
What the bar's tooltip reads. `{index}`, `{id}`, `{name}`, `{name-or-index}` and
`{workspace-name}`, the same tokens as the pager's `label`. Unset shows the workspace
and its monitor.

^[_A-Za-z][_A-Za-z0-9-]*\\.[_A-Za-z][_A-.description: A third-party applet found through its `.desktop` file (`Implements=me.aresa.Glimpse.Applet1`).

applet.description: The desktop-file id, e.g. `me.aresa.GlimpseTodo` for the todo example.

env.description: Variables set for the applet process on top of the panel's environment.

options.description: Passed to the applet as written.

animation-speed.description:
How fast every animation runs: `1.0` is normal, `2.0` twice as fast, `0.5` half as fast,
and `0` turns animations off. Anything else below `0.1` is refused, because a fade that
slow leaves the panel ignoring clicks while it runs. The popover and notification fades and every CSS transition
that reads `--gl-duration` follow it; the wallpaper keeps its own `transition-ms`.

auto-dark.description:
What decides the desktop mode: `auto` turns dark at sunset and light at sunrise where you
are, `system` follows the color scheme preference set elsewhere, for example in GNOME Settings.

blur.description:
Which parts of glimpse blur what is behind them: `panel`, `popover`, `notification`, or
`all`. Needs compositor support; without it they stay solid. Setup notes:
https://alex-oleshkevich.github.io/glimpse/config/services/appearance#blur

color-scheme.description:
Whether glimpse's own surfaces are light or dark. `auto` follows the desktop mode that
`auto-dark` decides; `light` and `dark` hold glimpse in one scheme whatever the desktop does.

theme.description:
The theme directory to load stylesheets from, looked up under `~/.config/glimpse/themes`
first and the installed themes second.

theme-variant.description:
A CSS class added to every window, so one theme can ship several looks. Letters, digits,
`-` and `_` only, not starting with a digit; anything else is ignored with a warning.

Backdrop.description:
A second background surface, named `glimpse-backdrop`, shown only where the compositor has
somewhere to place it — niri's Overview, through a `place-within-backdrop` layer rule.

blur-radius.description: Gaussian blur radius in output pixels; 0 blurs nothing.

downscale-factor.description:
Divides the output's physical size to get the size the backdrop is decoded at; 1 decodes
at full size. The shorter side never drops below 256 pixels.

enabled.description: Whether the backdrop surface is created at all.

image.description: Source image. Unset derives it from `[wallpaper] image`.

image-dark.description: Source image under the dark color scheme. Unset derives it from `[wallpaper] image-dark`.

BackdropOutput.description:
A per-output override of `[wallpaper.backdrop]`. Every field is optional and falls back to
the corresponding value in `[wallpaper.backdrop]` when unset.

hide-unnamed.description:
Whether to hide nearby devices that advertise no name. Most of them are beacons whose only
identity is their own address, and they arrive in large numbers during a scan.

scan-timeout.description:
How many seconds a scan for nearby devices runs before stopping on its own. Scanning costs
battery and interferes with connected audio, so it is never left running. `0` disables the
timeout and leaves the scan running until the popover closes.

ddc.description:
Whether glimpse controls the brightness of external monitors. Most monitors support it; turn
it off if one reacts slowly, flickers or misbehaves when the brightness changes.

minimum.description:
The lowest percent a display's backlight is allowed to reach; the keyboard backlight ignores
it and may still go to 0. Every write glimpse makes to a display source is clamped here,
because a screen driven all the way dark is indistinguishable from one that has failed.

Calendar.description:
Where calendar events come from. One list, read by every surface that shows an event: the
clock popover, the day markers on its grid, and the `next-event` applet.

poll-interval.description:
How often a source that lives on the network is fetched again, in seconds, unless it
names its own. Anything local is watched instead and ignores this: a `directory`, and an
`ical` whose `uri` is a path or a `file://`. The exception is a `file://` holding a
one-line feed URL, which is both — watched for the URL changing, fetched on this interval
for the calendar behind it.

sources.description: The sources themselves. Every one listed is active; remove it to stop reading it.

Chip.description:
One chip the system-monitor applet can show on the bar. Disk is deliberately not a variant —
arbitrarily many configured paths don't reduce to one chip value, so disk stays popover-only.

Clipboard.description:
What the panel remembers of the clipboard. The history lives in the panel process and in memory
only: it survives nothing, which is deliberate for a buffer that routinely holds passwords.

capture-images.description:
Whether images are captured as well as text. Off records text only; an image copied while
off is not recorded at all rather than recorded without its content.

enabled.description:
Whether the clipboard is watched at all. Off means no compositor connection is opened and
nothing is recorded; the applet then renders as if nothing had ever been copied.

limit.description:
How many entries are kept. Pinned entries do not count against it and are never evicted, so
a history full of pins holds more than this many. Clamped to 1..=10000.

max-entry-kib.description:
The largest single entry that will be captured, in kibibytes. Another application chooses
what it puts on the clipboard, so this is what stops one handing over something enormous.
Clamped to 4..=2048: the compositor read is capped at 2 MiB, and a larger value here would
promise a size that is discarded before it ever reaches the history.

max-total-kib.description:
The total the history may occupy, in kibibytes. Reached, the oldest unpinned entry is
dropped. This bounds memory in a way `limit` alone cannot, because one image can outweigh a
hundred lines of text. Clamped to 64..=1048576.

date-format.description: `{day}` is the day of the month with its ordinal suffix, e.g. "3rd".

enabled.description: Whether the clock shows on the lock stage at all.

time-format.description: A `strftime` pattern for the time, e.g. `%H:%M` or `%-I:%M %p`.

oneOf.description: `cmyk(0% 62% 72% 12%)`, a naive conversion with no color profile.

format.description:
The notation a picked color is copied in, and the one the palette shows it in. Every other
notation stays one click away in the palette.

limit.description:
How many colors the palette keeps, newest first. A pick beyond it drops the oldest.
Clamped to 1..=64.

FileTemplate.description: A strftime pattern naming a saved capture.

oneOf.description:
The image at its own size, centred on color, downscaled only when it exceeds the
output. contain enlarges a small image and looks soft; this is the honest option.

Geolocation.description:
Where you are, for sunset times and the local forecast. `geoclue` asks the system location
service; `manual` uses the `latitude` and `longitude` written beside it, which are then required.

HourFormat.description: How a time of day reads.

oneOf.description: Follow `LC_TIME`, which is what the locale's own `%X` resolves to.

enabled.description: Whether the idle timers run at all.

profiles.description:
The listeners to run on AC power and on battery. The battery profile applies while UPower
reports the machine on battery; without UPower the AC profile always applies.

respect-inhibitors.description:
Whether an app holding the screen awake, such as a video player or a browser playing a
video, pauses the listeners. A listener's own `respect-inhibitors` overrides this.

labels.description:
The text the panel shows for a layout, keyed by the layout's code or full name, matched
without regard to case: `{ "English (US)" = "EN", ua = "УКР" }`. Unlisted layouts show
their code.

remember.description:
Where a layout choice sticks: `window` gives each window its own layout, `app` shares one
per application, and `global` keeps one layout for everything.

on-idle.description: The shell command run when the timeout passes, e.g. `loginctl lock-session`.

on-resume.description: The shell command run on the next input after `on-idle` ran. Empty runs nothing.

timeout.description: Seconds without input before `on-idle` runs. `0` disables the listener.

background.description: The image and color behind the lock stage.

clock.description: The large time and date on the lock stage.

media.description: The now-playing transport, when something is playing.

notifications.description: Notifications received while the screen is locked.

pam-service.description: The PAM service that checks the password, read from `/etc/pam.d/<name>`.

prompt-output.description: `"focused"` follows the compositor's focused output; anything else is a connector name.

session.description: The suspend, reboot and power-off actions offered from the lock stage.

status.description: The status island: weather, battery, keyboard layout, bluetooth and network.

LockBackground.description: The lock stage's background: an image over a color, blurred and dimmed.

blur-radius.description: Gaussian blur radius in output pixels; 0 blurs nothing.

color.description:
Painted under everything: the whole background when no image resolves, and what shows
through `contain`'s letterbox.

dim.description: How much the background is darkened, from 0 (untouched) to 1 (black).

dim-dark.description: Overrides `dim` under the dark color scheme.

fit.description: How the image meets an output of a different aspect ratio.

image.description:
The background image, used as-is or under the light color scheme when `image-dark` is set.
With neither this nor `image-dark` set, the lock shows `[wallpaper]`'s `image` and
`image-dark`.

image-dark.description: The background image under the dark color scheme. Falls back to `image` when unset.

LockNotifications.description: Which notifications reach the lock stage, and how much of each one is shown.

enabled.description: Whether notifications show on the lock stage at all.

privacy.description:
A locked screen never shows a notification's body. `count` shows only a total; `apps`
also names which applications sent them.

LockPrivacy.description: How much of a notification's own content shows on the lock stage.

oneOf.description: Only a total count, naming nothing about any individual notification.
Also names which application each notification came from, never a summary or body.

LockSection.description: A lock stage element with nothing to configure besides whether it shows at all.

enabled.description: Whether this element shows on the lock stage at all.

LockSession.description: The session actions offered from the lock stage.

actions.description: Every action here is also gated by logind: one it refuses does not appear even when listed.

enabled.description: Whether the session actions show on the lock stage at all.

LockSessionAction.description: One system action offered from the lock stage.

oneOf.description: Suspend the system.
Reboot the system.
Power the system off.

bottom.description: Pixels between the panel and the bottom screen edge.

left.description: Pixels between the panel and the left screen edge.

right.description: Pixels between the panel and the right screen edge.

top.description: Pixels between the panel and the top screen edge.

Mpris.description:
Which media players the panel service follows, and what it does with their artwork. There are no
players here: every `org.mpris.MediaPlayer2.*` on the session bus is followed unless `ignore`
says otherwise.

art-max-kib.description:
The largest artwork that will be downloaded, in kibibytes. A player chooses this URL, so the
cap is what stops one pointing the service at something enormous. It bounds downloads only;
artwork a player names as a local file is bounded by its pixel dimensions instead, when it is
decoded. Clamped to 16..=65536.

fetch-art.description:
Whether artwork named by an `http` or `https` URL is downloaded. Players that name a local
file are unaffected, and turning this off leaves those working. Downloads go to
`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/glimpse/art/` and are capped by `art-max-kib`.

ignore.description:
Media players to keep off the bar. Write part of the player's name, as it appears in the
popover: `ignore = ['Firefox', 'chromium']` hides Firefox and every Chromium window
playing sound. Upper and lower case must match the name; start an entry with `(?i)` to
ignore case, as in `'(?i)firefox'`. Use single quotes around each entry.

hide-unnamed.description:
Whether to hide networks that broadcast no name. They cannot be joined by tapping them —
a hidden network is reached by typing its name in — so a row for one is unactionable.

scan-timeout.description:
How many seconds a scan for nearby networks runs before stopping on its own. Scanning
interrupts traffic on the same radio, so it is never left running. `0` disables the timeout
and leaves the scan running until the popover closes.

end-time.description: When the warm color ends under `schedule = "schedule"`, as `HH:MM` local time.

schedule.description:
When the screen warms: `automatic` from sunset to sunrise where you are, `schedule`
between `start-time` and `end-time`, `off` never.

start-time.description: When the warm color starts under `schedule = "schedule"`, as `HH:MM` local time.

temperature.description: The color temperature at night, in kelvin. Lower is warmer; 6500 is the screen's own color.

transition-minutes.description: How many minutes the change between day and night color takes.

edge.description: The corner or edge of the monitor popups stack from.

enabled.description: Whether new notifications pop up on screen. Turned off, they still go to the history.

hide-delay.description:
Seconds a popup stays when the sending app leaves its lifetime to the shell, which most do.
Hovering a popup pauses the countdown.

keep.description:
How many notifications are kept once they have been read. Dismissing one puts it here
rather than destroying it, which is what makes an accidental dismissal recoverable; past
this many, the oldest is dropped for good. Senders choose how often they notify, so this
is the bound that stops a chatty one growing the provider's memory without limit. Clamped
to 1..=1000.

max-items.description: How many popups show at once.

monitor.description:
The connector name of the monitor popups appear on, e.g. `DP-1`. Unset, or naming a
monitor that is not connected, uses the focused monitor.

suppress.description:
Regex patterns matched against the application identity, application name, title and body.
Matching notifications are not stored or published.

PagerMode.description:
What each slot stands for: `workspaces` for one slot per workspace, `windows` for one slot per
window on the current workspace.

PagerScope.description:
How much of the session the strip covers: `current` for only the workspace the user is on,
`output` for the workspaces on this panel's monitor, `session` for every workspace on every
monitor.

PagerShape.description:
How a slot is drawn: `dots` for a dot each with the current one drawn longer, which takes
the least room on the bar, or `labels` for the slot's label in a pill.

center.description: Applet names for the middle of the panel.

left.description: Applet names for the start of the panel: the left end, or the top on a side panel.

margin.description: Space in pixels between the panel and the screen edges.

monitor.description:
The connector name of the one monitor this panel appears on, e.g. `eDP-1`. Unset puts a
copy of the panel on every monitor.

position.description: The screen edge the panel sits on.

right.description: Applet names for the end of the panel: the right end, or the bottom on a side panel.

size.description: The panel's thickness in pixels: its height on a top or bottom edge, its width on a side.

Place.description:
Where a weather applet looks. Tagged on `at`, matching the shape `WatchPlace` takes, so a
place reads the same in a document and on the wire.

oneOf.description: Follow the geolocation service, and move with it.
A fixed pair of coordinates in degrees.

latitude.description: Degrees north of the equator, between -90 and 90.

longitude.description: Degrees east of Greenwich, between -180 and 180.

oneOf.description:
Resolve a city and ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code through Open-Meteo. This sends a
geocoding request to Open-Meteo, which receives the machine's public IP address.

name.description: City and country code, written as `City, CC`.

oneOf.description: A fixed pair of coordinates in degrees.

latitude.description: Degrees north of the equator, between -90 and 90.

longitude.description: Degrees east of Greenwich, between -180 and 180.

network.description: Whether network shares are watched and listed. Turns off one directory read.

trash.description: Whether the trash is watched and listed. Turns off one persistent inotify watch.

Printing.description: The printing service: how often it polls CUPS for job state, and which server it polls.

poll-active.description:
How often the service polls CUPS while a job is active, in seconds. Must be at least 1;
`0` would leave the poll timer with no interval to tick on.

poll-idle.description:
How often the service polls CUPS while no job is active, in seconds. Must be at least 1,
for the same reason as `poll-active`.

server-url.description:
The CUPS server to poll, such as `http://localhost:631/`. Unset uses CUPS's own default
server.

PrintingShow.description: When the printing chip is on the bar.

oneOf.description: The chip stays on the bar whenever a printer exists, idle or not.
The chip appears only while a print job is active or a printer needs attention.

listeners.description:
Each listener runs a command once the session has been idle for its `timeout`. Setting this
list replaces the default listeners rather than adding to them.

ac.description: The listeners used on AC power.

oneOf.description: Open-Meteo, which needs no account and no key.

The Norwegian Meteorological Institute, which needs no key either but asks for a
User-Agent naming the application. It is the only source that carries official warnings.

Regional.description:
What language this session reads, and how it writes a time of day and a measurement. Every
setting here defaults to what the environment already says, so an empty table is the right
answer on a machine whose locale is set up.

hour-format.description:
How a time of day reads wherever glimpse composes one itself — the world clock, the times
inside event rows, sunrise and sunset. A `strftime` format you write yourself, such as the
clock applet's `label-format`, is yours and is not affected by this.

language.description:
The language glimpse's text is shown in, such as `ru` for Russian. Empty uses your system
language. It changes only the words: dates, the clock and units still follow your system
settings. Takes effect the next time glimpse starts, for example when you log in.

units.description:
Whether temperatures, wind speeds and rainfall are reported in metric or imperial units.
Every reading in one weather report uses the same system, and the panel prints the symbols
that go with it.

capacity-interval.description:
Seconds between free-space samples of mounted removable volumes. `0` turns the capacity
readout off and runs no timer.

history-limit.description:
How many measurements history keeps, newest first. A measurement beyond it drops the
oldest. Clamped to 1..=64.

Screenshot.description: Screenshots. `glimpse-shot` reads it for where a capture is saved and how the editor opens.

color.description: The color annotation tools start with.

cursor.description: Include the pointer in a capture.

delay.description: Seconds to wait before capturing. Clamped to 0..=60.

directory.description: Where a capture is saved, created on first save. Unset means `$XDG_PICTURES_DIR/Screenshots`.

editor.description: Where an annotation opens: over the screen, or in a window.

filename.description:
The file name, as a strftime pattern expanded at the capture time. Must end in `.png` and
contain no `/`.

notify.description: Post a notification after a capture is saved.

stroke.description: The stroke width annotation tools start with.

color.description: The dot beside this calendar's events, as a hex color.

id.description:
What this source is called internally. It has to be unique, and it is what an event
carries so a surface can tell which calendar it came from.

name.description: What to call this calendar on screen. Unset falls back to `id`.

poll-interval.description:
How often to fetch this one, in seconds, overriding the shared interval. Ignored by a
source that is watched rather than fetched, the way the shared one is.

type.description: Whether `uri` names a subscription feed or a directory of `.ics` files.

uri.description:
The feed or directory. `webcal://`, which is what a provider's Subscribe button hands
out, is read as the `https://` it stands for. A provider's iCalendar URL behaves like a
read-only access token — anyone holding it can usually read the calendar without signing
in — so a `file://` path to a one-line sidecar file is offered as an alternative to
writing a secret URL into a configuration file that gets shared or committed.

oneOf.description:
One iCalendar document: an `https://` or `webcal://` feed, a local `.ics`, or a `file://`
holding a one-line feed URL. A local one is watched; a remote one is fetched on
`poll-interval`.
A directory of `.ics` files, watched for changes rather than polled.

SystemMonitor.description:
The system-monitor service: what it samples and how often. Whether it samples at all is not a
key here — it is derived from panel placement (see `placed_kinds`), because a poll interval
only means something once something is actually placed to consume it.

disk-paths.description:
Filesystem paths sampled for free space, each becoming its own popover tile. A path that
does not exist is skipped. An unmounted-but-present path still resolves — `statvfs` reports
whichever filesystem currently owns the directory, the same way `df` would — accepted, not
a bug. Each entry must be absolute; duplicates (after stripping a trailing `/`) collapse to
their first occurrence.

gpu.description: Whether to probe for an amdgpu GPU at all.

poll-interval.description: Seconds between samples of every reading this service publishes. Must be between 1 and 60.

Timezone.description: One zone in the clock popover's world clock.

icon.description: An icon name replacing the sun or moon the row picks from the hour it is showing.

label.description: What the row is called, such as `Tokyo`.

note.description:
A note after the `tomorrow` or `yesterday` the row works out for itself, such as
`the office`.

timezone.description: The IANA zone the row reads, such as `Asia/Tokyo`.

Transition.description: How one wallpaper image replaces another.

oneOf.description: A cut, with no animation.
A crossfade between the outgoing and incoming image.

Units.description: Which units every reading is reported in.

oneOf.description:
Follow `LC_MEASUREMENT`. Every locale glibc ships is metric except `en_US`, so this is
metric unless the machine is set to American English.
Celsius, kilometres per hour, millimetres.
Fahrenheit, miles per hour, inches.

color.description:
Painted under everything: the whole wallpaper when no image resolves, and what shows
through `contain`'s letterbox.

fit.description: How the image meets an output of a different aspect ratio.

image.description: The wallpaper image, used as-is or under the light color scheme when `image-dark` is set.

image-dark.description: The wallpaper image under the dark color scheme. Falls back to `image` when unset.

outputs.description:
Per-output overrides, matched by connector name such as `DP-1` (the same name
`[[panels]] monitor` takes). An output with no entry here
renders the values above. When two entries name the same connector, the first one wins.

transition-ms.description: Duration of that transition, in milliseconds.

WallpaperOutput.description:
A per-output override of the wallpaper (and backdrop) shown on one connector. Every field but
`monitor` is optional and falls back to the corresponding value in `[wallpaper]`, or
`[wallpaper.backdrop]` for the nested `backdrop` fields, when unset.

monitor.description: The connector this override applies to, e.g. `"DP-2"`.

Weather.description:
How a forecast is fetched. There are no places here: a place is registered by whatever wants to
see it, through `WatchPlace`, and held for as long as it keeps asking. Nothing is fetched and
no location is resolved until something does.

forecast-days.description: How many days the daily forecast covers, today included. Clamped to 1..=10.

poll-interval.description:
How often a forecast is fetched again, in seconds. The provider recomputes current
conditions every fifteen minutes, so anything shorter asks again for data that has not
moved; the provider's `Refresh` method is how a person asks for it now. Values below 600 are raised.

provider.description: Which service a forecast comes from. `open-meteo` needs no account and no key.
